questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The bank refused to ______ the loan because the applicant had a poor credit history.' (A) sanction (B) cancel (C) deposit (D) invest

options.option_text: cancel (end existing loan, not refuse new)

questions.explanation: SANCTION (verb) = to officially approve or authorise. In banking: 'sanction a loan' = formally grant/approve a loan after credit assessment. Sentence says the bank REFUSED to sanction — meaning it declined to grant the loan. CANCEL would refer to stopping an existing loan — not applicable when a new loan application is refused. DEPOSIT = putting money in an account — opposite direction to lending. INVEST = deploying capital for returns — not the bank's action here. WORD FAMILY: sanction (noun) = approval OR punitive measure (contextual); sanctioned (adj) = approved. COLLOCATIONS: 'sanction a loan', 'receive sanction', 'loan sanctioned.' ANTONYM in context: 'rejected' or 'declined' (synonyms for the bank's action). CLOZE TEST STRATEGY: (1) Read full sentence for meaning. (2) Identify the SUBJECT and OBJECT. (3) Eliminate options that don't fit grammatically. (4) Among remaining, pick the one that matches the exact banking context. PYQ FREQUENCY: banking vocabulary (sanction, disburse, collateral, moratorium, NPA) appears in every IBPS PO, SBI PO, RRB Officer English cloze test.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: 'The government announced a ______ on loan repayments to provide relief to farmers during the drought.' (A) moratorium (B) premium (C) dividend (D) subsidy

options.option_text: subsidy (financial aid, not specifically on loan repayments)

questions.explanation: MORATORIUM = a temporary suspension or postponement of an activity (especially repayment of debts). 'Moratorium on loan repayments' = farmers allowed to temporarily stop paying EMIs. RECENT CONTEXT: RBI COVID-19 moratorium (March-August 2020) — 6-month EMI holiday for all term loans. PREMIUM = extra charge (insurance premium, risk premium) — opposite of relief. DIVIDEND = portion of profit distributed to shareholders — no connection to loan repayments. SUBSIDY = government financial assistance to reduce the cost of goods/services — while close to 'relief', it doesn't specifically mean suspending loan repayment obligations. WORD ORIGIN: Moratorium from Latin 'morari' = to delay. UPSC ANGLE: Moratorium is a tool used by central banks during economic crises — tested in RBI Grade B, NABARD mains. PYQ FREQUENCY: moratorium appears in IBPS PO Mains English, SBI PO Mains cloze tests frequently — especially post-2020. EXAM TRAP: subsidy is plausible but incorrect — subsidy is a direct financial grant, not a deferral of obligation.

questions.stem: Choose the correct pair for the double blank: 'The ______ of non-performing assets has become a ______ challenge for public sector banks.' (A) surge / formidable (B) decline / trivial (C) surge / negligible (D) decline / formidable

options.option_text: surge / negligible (logic mismatch — surge but negligible)

questions.explanation: DOUBLE BLANK STRATEGY: both blanks must be LOGICALLY CONSISTENT. 'Of non-performing assets has become a ___ challenge for banks' — if NPAs are rising (surge), the challenge is big (formidable). If NPAs are declining (decline), the challenge would be small (trivial). VALID PAIRS: (surge + formidable) or (decline + trivial). INVALID PAIRS: (surge + negligible) = contradiction — rising problem can't be negligible. (decline + formidable) = contradiction — falling problem shouldn't be formidable. VOCABULARY: NPA (Non-Performing Asset) = a loan on which the borrower has not been paying interest or principal for more than 90 days. SURGE = rapid increase. FORMIDABLE = inspiring fear/respect due to size or difficulty. NEGLIGIBLE = so small as to be unimportant. UPSC ANGLE: NPA crisis in Indian banking — PSBs (public sector banks) had NPA ratio peaking at ~11% in 2018; brought down through IBC (Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code). PYQ FREQUENCY: double-blank cloze with economic/banking vocabulary in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains 5-10 blanks per passage. EXAM TRAP: option D (decline + formidable) — students pick formidable as it sounds 'serious' without checking the first blank.

questions.stem: Fill: 'Despite repeated warnings, the company continued to ______ regulations, resulting in a heavy fine.' (A) flout (B) follow (C) amend (D) uphold
questions.explanation: FLOUT = to openly disregard a rule, law, or convention. 'Flout regulations' = blatantly ignore/violate rules despite knowing them. Sentence: the company was warned but continued to FLOUT (ignore) regulations → got fined. FOLLOW, UPHOLD = antonyms — obey/support rules, so a fine would NOT result. AMEND = change/modify — not the same as violating. CONFUSABLE PAIR — FLAUNT vs FLOUT: FLAUNT = to show off proudly ('flaunted his wealth'). FLOUT = to disregard openly ('flouted traffic rules'). These are a classic confusable pair tested in IBPS PO. MEMORY AID: 'FLOUT = break-out from rules.' 'FLAUNT = show-it-all-to-taunt.' USAGE: 'flouting the law', 'flouting norms', 'flouting regulations' — all appear in legal/corporate news. PYQ FREQUENCY: flaunt/flout confusion + cloze banking passage in IBPS PO English, SSC CGL Tier 2 English 1-2× per cycle. EXAM TRAP: students write 'flaunt' when asked for the word meaning 'violate rules' — wrong; flaunt = show off.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The Reserve Bank of India decided to ______ the interest rate to curb inflation.' (A) hike (B) waive (C) defer (D) freeze

options.option_text: hike (raise the rate — a classic anti-inflation tool)
waive (cancel/remove the rate — opposite of curbing)
defer (postpone — not a monetary policy tool to reduce inflation)
freeze (keep constant — doesn't actively curb inflation)

questions.explanation: MONETARY POLICY LOGIC: When INFLATION is high, the RBI RAISES (HIKES) the repo rate → borrowing becomes expensive → people spend less → demand falls → inflation cools. 'Hike the interest rate to curb inflation' = standard RBI tool. WAIVE = cancel entirely — would mean zero interest rate, which STIMULATES spending, worsening inflation. DEFER = postpone — not applicable to rate adjustments. FREEZE = keep at current level — neutral action, doesn't actively curb inflation. UPSC ANGLE: Repo rate (rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks), Reverse repo rate, SLR, CRR — all monetary policy instruments. RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meets 6 times a year. REVERSE ACTION: when inflation is low/economy slows, RBI CUTS repo rate. KEY COLLOCATIONS: 'hike rates', 'cut rates', 'hold rates steady', 'signal a pause.' PYQ FREQUENCY: RBI monetary policy vocabulary (repo, hike, cut, liquidity, inflation) appears in EVERY IBPS PO, SBI PO, RBI Grade B English cloze passage. EXAM TRAP: 'freeze' sounds plausible (keeping inflation from rising) but doesn't describe what the RBI does to curb it — hiking is the correct action.

questions.stem: Fill: 'The audit report revealed that funds meant for infrastructure were ______ to private accounts.' (A) diverted (B) allocated (C) disbursed (D) credited

options.option_text: disbursed (formally paid out — implies legitimate payment)

questions.explanation: DIVERT (funds) = to redirect money from its intended purpose to another, typically illegal, purpose. The sentence says funds MEANT FOR INFRASTRUCTURE went to PRIVATE ACCOUNTS — this is a classic financial fraud/misappropriation pattern. DIVERT = the correct word as it implies wrongful redirection. ALLOCATE = to officially assign resources to a purpose — no wrongdoing; wouldn't result in an audit finding of concern. DISBURSE = to pay out officially (e.g., government disburses grants) — implies legitimate payment. CREDIT = to add to an account (bank credits salary) — neutral, no fraud implied. UPSC ANGLE: Diversion of funds is a key concept in CAG audit reports. CAG (Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Art 148) regularly flags 'diversion of funds' in state government audits. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'divert/diversion' appears in IBPS PO Mains, NABARD, RBI Grade B English — especially in passages about financial irregularities. EXAM TRAP: 'disbursed to private accounts' sounds grammatically fine but misses the wrongful-redirection implication that the audit context demands.

questions.stem: Choose the word that BEST completes: 'The bank's decision to ______ the loan application was seen as ______, given that the applicant met all eligibility criteria.' (A) reject / arbitrary (B) approve / arbitrary (C) reject / prudent (D) approve / prudent

options.option_text: reject / arbitrary (rejecting despite eligibility = without reason = arbitrary)
approve / arbitrary (approving eligible = reasonable, not arbitrary)
reject / prudent (rejecting without cause is not prudent — it's arbitrary)
approve / prudent (approving eligible applicant is prudent but that's the expected outcome)

questions.explanation: LOGIC CHAIN: Applicant met ALL eligibility criteria → bank REJECTED → this rejection was seen as ______ (how?). Rejection despite full eligibility = UNREASONABLE, UNJUSTIFIED = ARBITRARY. ARBITRARY = based on whim or random choice rather than reason or logic. PRUDENT = showing care and thought for the future; wise. Rejecting an eligible applicant is NOT prudent (it's actually bad banking practice — prudent banking means fair credit assessment). APPROVE / ARBITRARY: approving an eligible person is the REASONABLE thing to do — not arbitrary. APPROVE / PRUDENT: approving an eligible person is indeed prudent, but the sentence says the decision was seen as ______ (negative implication from 'given that criteria was met'). VOCABULARY: arbitrary (adj, from Latin 'arbitrarius' = depending on individual judgment). UPSC ANGLE: 'arbitrary' is a key legal term — Art 14 (Equality before law) forbids arbitrary state action. Arbitrariness test used in many SC judgments. PYQ FREQUENCY: double-blank cloze testing logic + vocabulary in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains, RBI Grade B English — typically 5 blanks per passage.
